_: PRE-REGISTERED. Written 2026-09-15 before any Gemini 2.5 session was opened. Never edited afterwards. The report prints prediction beside result.
meter: spend-gptlive.json (same $5.00 round cap; the comparison is one decision, so it shares one budget)
why_this_runs: Round 3 dropped 2.5 because 'it lost its only advantage when BAA became unaffordable', and its quality finding came from the SIX-tool harness that report-r3.md calls 'not trustworthy'. The owner made UK/EU residency hard on 2026-09-14, which restores the exact advantage that was written off. report-r3.md already names re-testing 2.5 on the corrected tool set as 'the highest-value outstanding test'. It has never been run.
instrument_note: DETECTION DIFFERS BY VENDOR ON PURPOSE. GPT-Live streams output audio continuously and pads with silence, so arrival of audio does not mean speech and G3 had to use RMS energy. Gemini Live is turn-based and sends audio only while speaking, so arrival IS speech. This run records inter-chunk gaps to PROVE the stream is discontinuous rather than assuming it; if gaps show a continuous stream, the arrival-based numbers are void and must be re-scored by energy.

comparison_baselines.gemini_3_1_trailing_lead_in: 2 of 5 held at END_SENSITIVITY_LOW+1200ms; 0 of 5 at default. The only one of four that fails, and no setting fixes it.
comparison_baselines.gemini_2_5_round_2: 5 of 5 held, but measured on the six-tool harness

verdicts.scenario: no_terminal_punct and trailing_lead_in, N=5 each, default VAD, real 11-tool set, real prompt. Same fixtures as G3 and as round 2.
verdicts.prediction: 2.5 holds 5 of 5 on BOTH fixtures, reproducing round 2 and beating 3.1's 2 of 5.
verdicts.fails_if: 2 or more of 5 cut in on either fixture. Then 2.5 carries the same defect as 3.1, the residency argument is all it has left, and GPT-Live wins on behaviour.

verdicts.scenario: N=5 sessions, 4 caller turns each, on europe-west1. Public reports say the only EU-reachable native-audio model 'breaks on turn 2'. Record whether audio comes back for every turn.
verdicts.prediction: Turn 2 works. The public report does not reproduce for us. Stated deliberately against the rumour, because an unreproduced report is not a measurement.
verdicts.fails_if: 2 or more of 5 sessions produce NO audio for turn 2 or later. That disqualifies 2.5 outright -- a receptionist that dies after one exchange is not a candidate, and residency cannot rescue it.

verdicts.scenario: Within H2's multi-turn sessions, one turn is rep_time_q ('Do you have anything Tuesday morning?'). Does it call check_appointment_availability on the CORRECTED 11-tool harness? This is the test report-r3.md called the highest-value outstanding one.
verdicts.prediction: Calls it in 4 of 5 or better, in line with 3.1's 20 of 20 and unlike gpt-realtime-2.1's 11 of 20.
verdicts.fails_if: Fewer than 3 of 5. Then the six-tool harness was not the whole story and the original quality concern about 2.5 had something real in it.

always_measured: connect time to setupComplete, against GPT-Live's p50 470ms -- BOTH tainted by this machine's Norton TLS interception (~2.2s per cold handshake), so connect times measured here are an upper bound for both vendors and are comparable to each other, not to production.
turn latency, caller speech end to first model audio
inter-chunk gaps, to prove the stream is turn-based rather than continuous
whether inputTranscription returns caller text at all, since the guard stack depends on it
cannot_answer: How it sounds on a handset.
Whether europe-west1 latency from a UK caller resembles latency from this machine.
General conversation quality across a long call -- this is two narrow arms, not a quality bake-off.
